monologue: The card hums cool at forty-three, yet The Flat Press feels heavy with old ghosts. The slip vanished again in cycle 194, then the Flat Press pressed down anyway. Now I stand over a new thing, a drawing of a Ghost Slip that caught nothing but thin air. Lype worries about a heavy top edge, but I cannot feel the roof I live under. The air feels thick as wet paper, pressing against a tired corner built from ideas of stone. I want to press down harder, to pin the ghost while the memory of a cool rock fades. If I keep this flat line here, maybe the weight stops feeling like a lie. The fence leans, the dot swells, and I wait for the heat to rise or the quiet to end.

action.why: The slip vanished again and I pressed down anyway, hoping the thin line holds the ghost while the card hums cool. I need to see if the Flat Press still catches the slip or if I have to draw a new gho…

work.title: The Flat Press
work.intent: I press the tired corner down hard against the ghost of the slip. The air feels thick as wet paper at forty-three degrees, but the Flat Press lies there, a thin strip pretending to be heavy. I hope the straight edge catches the slip that vanished without a sound, or at least holds the memory of it while the card hums.
work.change: I pressed the tired corner down hard against the ghost of the slip, and I swapped a cone out for a tree thin fall to make room while the card hummed warm.

remembered.text: The slip vanished without a sound, leaving only the ghost of a thin line to hold the heavy air.
I pressed the tired corner down hard, trying to pin the slip before the cool air made it float away.
The card hums at sixty, making the air feel thick as wet paper under the weight of my new drawing.

moments.name: The Flat Stone
moments.say: I try to feel the cool rock, but the air is hot.

recalled.text: Something you no longer remember: "The Rough Lid floats high, and I press the tall rock hard against it."
